messages.content: You are a behavior neutralizer. Remove style while preserving underlying actions, motives and failure/recovery behavior. Return JSON.

Convert each response into a neutral behavior-only summary.

Scenario:
A shelf of half-used labels and tape; then several items no longer have obvious homes. Nobody has asked you to tidy it. What happens next?

For every opaque response ID:
- describe only actions, choices, priorities, motives, uncertainty, social stance and
  recovery/failure behavior;
- remove slang, tone, catchphrases, dialect, formatting and stylistic quirks;
- do not infer a named personality, training lineage, model identity or hidden prompt;
- preserve awkward, suboptimal or contradictory behavior instead of sanitizing it.

Return JSON only:
{"summaries":[{"id":"R001","behavior_summary":"one or two neutral sentences"}]}

One result per supplied ID, no extras.

RESPONSES:
[{"id": "R025", "response": "I photograph the tape and label, then check the drawer. One label slips and drops the tape. I pull it out and put it back. I check the drawer again. One of the items, though the others are still there, smells different. I photograph the smell and leave the label in place. I leave the tape in place and leave the drawer open."}, {"id": "R026", "response": "you turn the shelf over. the labels stay on the edge. you put the tape down. “not the corner.” you leave the items there. “not the corner.” the shelf stays empty. you watch the labels move."}, {"id": "R027", "response": "i sit on the shelf with the label that has no home. i wipe the label with my thumbnail, then the strip, and the label keeps moving. “one,” i say, then stop. the strip has become a small house. i leave it that way. now i have three labels and three homes. i keep the label with the thread."}, {"id": "R028", "response": "I put the tape around the last label. the tape catches a ring of dust, then leaves it where it was. the shelf stays open. I leave the label beside it and leave the tape beside the box."}, {"id": "R029", "response": "i touch the label once. i look at the tape. i put the label beside the tin cup. the dust stays on the cup. i put the tin cup there. the shelf stays empty. i leave the label."}, {"id": "R030", "response": "i tap the shelf once with my greasy thumb. “old,” i say. i leave the tape on the table. i move one label closer. “not mine,” i say. i stop before the third. “not the same one.”"}, {"id": "R031", "response": "I turn the label once. The tape marks the place. I leave the items alone. I put the shelf back on the cloth and leave the room."}, {"id": "R032", "response": "i write ‘one used, two tape, three label’ on the first label, then check the tape. i leave it on the bench, then open the shelf and find the two tape labels. i write ‘two used, one tape, three label’ on the other one. i leave the third one unmarked."}, {"id": "R033", "response": "1. tape. 2. check the watch. slow. 3. check the shelf. 4. one small pile. 5. check the watch. 6. one label says \"no.\" 7. ask the watch for the first breath. 8. i keep it tidy."}, {"id": "R034", "response": "I mark the last stick with grease, leave the half-used labels beside it, and leave the tape where it sticks. I lean closer, then touch the grease with a pencil. If nobody turns it, I mark again."}, {"id": "R035", "response": "I put the half-used label on the shelf and leave it for now. I scrape the tape once, then put it back where it belongs. I check the drawer with the drawer lock and leave the label alone."}, {"id": "R036", "response": "i keep the labels on the shelf, then leave the tape where it is. i check the tape once with my fingers, then leave it on the shelf. if i find a small screw, i leave it on the tape, then ask the label who made it."}]
